linguistics.meaning: Victoria's Secret — literally ‘Victoria, she keeps it secret from her (obviative)’ / ‘the thing she keeps secret’

morphemes.gloss: borrowed proper noun: ‘Victoria’ — the personal name. In Plains Cree practice, English personal-names that lack a Cree calque are kept in Roman script inside an otherwise-syllabic phrase, exactly the way the plaque carves it.
3rd-person agent prefix: ‘he/she’ — the same o‑ that opens many VTA conjunct/independent forms when a third person is acting on a further-away (obviative) third person.
verb root: ‘to steal, to take by stealth, to do (something) secretly.’ The same root in kimôtiw ‘s/he steals,’ kimôtâpamêw ‘s/he secretly watches him,’ and the particle kîmôc ‘secretly, in stealth.’
stem extender / connective vowel string: links the steal-root to the relational endings that follow. Carries the long-â that gives the word its swung middle.
VTA stem-marker: the consonant that closes the steal-stem and opens the relational-suffix slot — same ‑m‑ that closes many VTA stems before the obviative tail (e.g. wâpam‑ ‘see’ → wâpamêw).
obviative theme-marker: signals that the goal of the verb is the further-away (4th-person / obviative) participant, not the speaker or hearer. The ‘her‑(obviative)’ slot.
obviative animate ending: ‘from her / by her (obviative).’ The same ‑wa that closes okosisiyiwa ‘his (obv) son’ and other obviative-marked forms.
verb stem: steal, take by stealth

relatedForms.note: The bare AI verb ‘s/he steals.’ Inside the headword the same kimôt‑ root carries the ‘keep secret / take by stealth’ reading.

morphemes.gloss: particle: ‘secretly, on the sly, in stealth.’ Same root family as the verb kimôt‑.

relatedForms.note: The free-standing adverbial form. Anchors the ‘secret / sly’ semantic field that the headword verb is built on.

relatedForms.english: S/he watches him/her secretly, s/he spies on him/her
relatedForms.note: Sister VTA verb in the same kimôt‑ family: same stealth root, different action. ‘To secretly watch / spy on someone.’ Confirms the productive use of kimôt‑ as a stealth modifier on other verb roots.

quickReference.english: Victoria's Secret — ‘Victoria, she keeps it secret from her’
quickReference.note: Headword on the plaque. Phrase: borrowed proper noun + VTA verb in obviative.
Free-standing adverbial particle from the same root family.

quickReference.english: S/he secretly watches / spies on him/her

The obviative-animate suffix family that closes the headword. Plains Cree marks a third-person ‘from her’ as further-away from the speaker than the basic 3rd person.

culturalStory.heading: About victoria okimôtânimiyiwa — Victoria's Secret
body: The Edmonton trail named ‘Victoria's Secret’ is named for the small, lacy-looking line of the same nickname in the local MTB network — a piece of techy bench-cut singletrack that drops east-west along the river just south of the 102 Ave bridge, with off-camber roots, a couple of switchbacks, and a hidden, somewhat-private feel to it that earns the joke. The English name predates the plaque by years among the local riders who built and maintain the line; the Cree name victoria okimôtânimiyiwa reads that joke back through Plains Cree morphology.

Built up, the phrase is ‘Victoria, she keeps it secret from her (obviative)’: the borrowed name victoria followed by a fully-Cree VTA verb in obviative — the 3rd-person prefix o‑, the steal/stealth root kimôt‑, the ‑âni‑/‑m‑/‑iyi‑/‑wa relational tail that places the ‘her’ (the secret-keeper's secret) one degree further away than the agent. Plains Cree obviation lets the language pin down whose secret it is and whose it is from in a way English needs an extra ‘from’ for. The result is a phrase that reads as a small piece of grammar in motion: a proper noun handed to a verb that does the work of marking the secret as Victoria's own.

The plaque carries that reading visually as well. A black silhouette in the shape of a bra fills the pale-blue plaque, but the cups are not blank — they are filled with a forested pine-and-hill landscape with a small switchback path through it. The trail itself, in other words, is hidden inside the joke. Underneath, the carved Cree text victoria okimôtânimiyiwa and the English ‘Victoria's Secret’ run side-by-side. The trail sits on ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory) in the Central Edmonton (North) river-valley network, near the Lovers Lane heart-plaque and the Wonder Woman silhouette — a small cluster of MTB-vernacular signs now also wearing a Plains Cree reading.

notes: PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE: The plaque is carved with the phrase 'victoria okimôtânimiyiwa' (Roman 'victoria' + Cree VTA verb in obviative). The current catalogue.json creeName is the placeholder 'vicSecret' and creeSyllabics is empty. Coordinator should update catalogue creeName → 'victoria okimôtânimiyiwa' and creeSyllabics → 'victoria ᐅᑭᒨᑖᓂᒥᔨᐘ' (Roman name kept, Cree verb in syllabics — mirroring the plaque exactly).

Morpheme bracketing of 'okimôtânimiyiwa' is mid-confidence. The verb has the unmistakable kimôt- (steal/stealth) root, the o- 3rd-person prefix, and the -iyi-/-wa obviative tail; the middle ‑âni‑/‑m‑ portion is treated here as stem-extender + VTA stem-marker for teaching clarity, but a stricter dictionary lookup may reanalyse it as a single ‑ânim‑ relational stem ('regard X as one's secret possession'). Either reading preserves the gloss 'she keeps it secret from her (obviative).'

Two near-identical 'Victoria's Secret' plaques are mounted on the wall (one on the upper-right cluster, one on the central-row cluster). The asset wired here is the canonical design render at victoriaSecret/Screenshot 2023-11-17 at 11.59.34 AM.png (copied to docs/assets/victoriaSecret/victoria_secret_render.png by the coordinator pre-stage).

Trailforks pick: HIGH confidence — Trailforks trail #10632 'Victoria's Secret' in Central Edmonton (North) Northwest Edmonton, Alberta. Trailhead 53.54268, -113.53953. The trail is part of the same river-valley cluster as Lovers Lane (#15796), Wonder Woman, and Purple Haze (#15797) — all of which appear on the wall as adjacent plaques. Sibling trails 'Victoria's Lower Secret' and 'Victoria's other secret' (#19734) also exist in the network but are clearly secondary spurs; the canonical 'Victoria's Secret' (#10632) is the line the plaque commemorates.

Map coordinates {53.54268, -113.53953} are the Trailforks-listed trailhead. No mapEndCoords or track populated — the trail is short (1.0 km / 3,338 ft) and largely east-west; a future revision could trace a polyline over satellite imagery.
